content: The Chief Veterinary Officer (CVO) is an official within the British government who serves as the head of veterinary services in the United Kingdom. Separate Chief Veterinary Officers also exist for Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland. The following individuals have held the position of Chief Veterinary Officer for the United Kingdom: Alexander Curtis Cope served from 1893 to 1905. Sir Stewart Stockman held the position from 1905 to 1926. Sir James Joseph Ralph Jackson served from 1926 to 1932. Sir Percy John Luxton Kelland was in office from 1932 to 1938. Sir Daniel Alfred Edmond Cabot served from 1938 to 1948. Sir Thomas Dalling held the role from 1948 to 1952. Sir John Neish Ritchie served from 1952 to 1965. Mr. John Reid was in office from 1965 to 1970. Mr. A.G. Beynon served from 1970 to 1973. Mr. A.C.L. Brown held the position from 1973 to 1980. Mr. William Howard Rees served from August 1980 to May 1988. Keith Meldrum was in office from June 1988 to April 1997. James Scudamore served from April 1997 to March 2004. Dr. Debby Reynolds has held the position since March 2004. For Wales, the Chief Veterinary Officer is Dr. Christianne Glossop. In Scotland, the position of Chief Veterinary Officer was established in October 2002. The following individuals have held this role: Leslie Gardner served from October 2002 to March 2003.
